queries.hook: The wish to understand what these texts teach, and to find in them something steady to lean on.
queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy.
queries.steady: The mind can be trained slowly, by practice and letting go; each time it wanders, it can be gently brought back.
queries.act: Bring the mind back each time it wanders, with practice and letting go; make the mind your friend through steady practice.
queries.story: A story of a student who came to a teacher with questions and was led, step by step, toward the truth.

hook.speaker: Krishna
hook.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
hook.sanskrit: शनैः शनैरुपरमेद् बुद्ध्या धृतिगृहीतया । आत्मसंस्थं मनः कृत्वा न किञ्चिदपि चिन्तयेत् ॥
hook.line: Little by little, with patience and steady resolve, settle the mind and let other thoughts go.
hook.translation: Little by little one should come to rest, with understanding held steady; fixing the mind on the self, one should think of nothing else.
hook.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on the power of understanding to end confusion and guilt.
alternates.sanskrit: तद्विद्धि प्रणिपातेन परिप्रश्नेन सेवया । उपदेक्ष्यन्ति ते ज्ञानं ज्ञानिनस्तत्त्वदर्शिनः ॥
alternates.line: Learn from those who have seen the truth: approach with humility, ask real questions, and serve.
alternates.translation: Learn it by bowing down, by questioning, and by service. Those who are wise and have seen the truth will teach you that knowledge.
alternates.why: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

prasang.title: The glory of knowledge
prasang.summary: Krishna praises knowledge: learn it humbly from those who know, it carries even the worst wrongdoer across, faith and self-control bring it, and doubt destroys. He ends: cut your doubt and stand up.
prasang.lesson: Learn humbly, trust the process, and cut through doubt to act.

alternates.speaker: Krishna
alternates.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
alternates.sanskrit: श्री भगवानुवाचअसंशयं महाबाहो मनो दुर्निग्रहं चलं । अभ्यासेन तु कौन्तेय वैराग्येण च गृह्यते ॥
alternates.line: Yes, the mind is restless and hard to hold. But practice and letting go can train it.
alternates.translation: The Blessed Lord said: Undoubtedly, mighty-armed one, the mind is restless and hard to control. But it is held by practice and by detachment, Kaunteya.
alternates.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.meaning: Krishna is teaching Arjuna how to sit with the mind. The mind wanders, and it will not stay still all at once. The instruction is to come to rest little by little. One holds understanding steady and fixes the mind on what is real, letting other thoughts go. It is a gentle, repeated settling, not a single forceful act.
verse.for_you: Your mind keeps running because it was never taught to stop. It is not a flaw. It is a habit of work and worry that has no switch. You do not need to push it down. You could come to rest little by little, with patience.
verse.scene_line: You are sitting in your quiet morning, and the mind is a lamp in a place where the wind has not yet stopped.
asks: How do I tell my mind to stop without fighting it?
Can I really let other thoughts go?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse.sanskrit: इन्द्रियाणां हि चरतां यन्मनोऽनुविधीयते । तदस्य हरति प्रज्ञां वायुर्नावमिवाम्भसि ॥
verse.line: When the mind chases a wandering sense, it is swept off like a boat in the wind.
verse.translation: When the mind runs after the roving senses, it carries away one's understanding, as the wind carries a boat away on the water.
verse.why: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

prasang.title: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

verse.meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna what a person of steady mind looks like, and Krishna answers by describing someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, and master of the senses. He then traces how this steadiness is lost: when the mind runs after the roving senses, it carries away one's understanding, as the wind carries a boat away on the water. The point is that steadiness is built by guarding attention, because anger and ruin start with what you dwell on.
verse.for_you: You are working with a mind that keeps chasing what is next, and that is exactly what Krishna describes. The restlessness you feel is not a lack of will. It is the wind taking the boat.
verse.try_today: Notice one moment when your attention drifts, and let it go without pulling it back.
verse.scene_line: You are in your own morning, and the wind is already taking the boat.
asks: How do I guard my attention without forcing it?
How do I know if I am content or just distracted?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse.line: Heat and cold, pleasure and pain come and go. They don't last; learn to bear them.
verse.translation: Contact of the senses with their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. They come and go and do not last. Bear them patiently, Arjuna.
verse.why: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.
verse.misuse: Bearing passing discomfort is not putting up with harm or abuse; those are not weather to wait out.

prasang.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

verse.meaning: Krishna speaks to Arjuna on the battlefield, telling him that the true self is never born and never dies, and that the body merely changes like old clothes. He says that contact between the senses and their objects brings cold and heat, pleasure and pain. These experiences come and go, and they do not last. The instruction is to bear these passing states patiently, because what you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.
verse.for_you: Your mind moves from one restless thought to the next because it is looking for a solid ground that is not there, and that ground is not in any passing feeling. The work is not to stop the weather, but to know that the sky remains.
verse.try_today: Notice one passing feeling without naming it good or bad.
verse.scene_line: You stand on the edge of your own morning, watching the weather of your mind move across you.
asks: How do I tell the self apart from the passing thought?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna on three kinds of food, effort, speech and giving.
verse.sanskrit: आयुःसत्त्वबलारोग्यसुखप्रीतिविवर्धनाः । रस्याः स्निग्धाः स्थिरा हृद्या आहाराः सात्त्विकप्रियाः ॥
verse.line: Food that builds life, strength, health, cheer and calm: that's the food of a clear mind.
verse.translation: Foods that increase life, vitality, strength, health, happiness and cheerfulness, that are flavourful, soothing, nourishing and agreeable, are dear to the sattvic.
verse.why: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

prasang.title: Three kinds of food, offering, austerity and giving
prasang.summary: Food, offering, austerity and giving each come in three kinds. Speech should be true, kind and helpful; giving should expect nothing back; effort for show doesn't last.
prasang.lesson: Speak kindly and truly, give without strings, and drop the show.

verse.meaning: Krishna is telling Arjuna about three kinds of food and three kinds of giving. He is explaining what a clear mind actually eats. Food that builds life, strength, health, cheer and calm is the food of a clear mind. It is not just about what is on the plate. It is about the nature of what you take in. The mind needs nourishment that steadies it. The verse proposes that the mind is fed by what is true, kind, and steady. You could choose what you feed it.
verse.for_you: Your mind is restless because it is being fed noise. It is trying to digest things that do not build life. Choose what you take in this morning. Let it be simple and true. Let your mind eat something that creates calm.
verse.try_today: Eat one thing that is plain and true, without distraction.
verse.scene_line: You are standing in a kitchen, choosing what to take into your body.
asks: How do I know if my food is building calm?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Arjuna asks which devotee is best; Krishna offers a ladder of practices.
verse.sanskrit: अथ चित्तं समाधातुं न शक्नोषि मयि स्थिरम् । अभ्यासयोगेन ततो मामिच्छाप्तुं धनञ्जय ॥
verse.line: If you can't keep your mind fixed yet, then reach for it through regular practice.
verse.translation: If you cannot fix your mind steadily on me, then seek to reach me by the yoga of practice, Dhananjaya.
verse.why: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

prasang.title: Form or formless: which devotee is best, and the ways to reach him
prasang.summary: Krishna says devotion to a personal form is easier, then offers a ladder: fix your mind; if not, practise; if not, work for me; if not, let go of results. Letting go brings peace at once.
prasang.lesson: If the ideal is too hard, take the next step down, and keep going.

verse.meaning: Arjuna asks Krishna which kind of devotee is the best, and Krishna offers a ladder of practices. He says fix your mind on me. If that is too hard, then reach for me through regular practice. The idea is plain: if the highest step is out of reach right now, take the next step down and keep walking. It is not a failure to not be steady today. It is simply a sign to begin where you are.
verse.for_you: Your work has trained you to solve, to move, to fix. But the mind that will not settle asks for a different kind of work, one that returns each day. The verse does not ask you to force stillness. It asks you to return.
verse.try_today: Let the first thought of the morning be a return to one practice you will do again tomorrow.
verse.scene_line: You are on the step just below the summit, and that is where the path begins.
asks: What is the one practice I can return to tomorrow morning?
How do I tell returning from forcing?
What does regular practice look like in my morning?

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna, who asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher.
verse.sanskrit: नियतं कुरु कर्म त्वं कर्म ज्यायो ह्यकर्मणः । शरीरयात्रापि च ते न प्रसिद्ध्येदकर्मणः ॥
verse.line: Do the work that's yours. Doing something beats doing nothing; even living needs action.
verse.translation: Do your allotted work, for action is better than inaction. Even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
verse.why: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

prasang.title: Why doing your duty without attachment is better
prasang.summary: Arjuna is confused and asks for one clear answer. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction.
prasang.lesson: Not acting is still a choice; do the work that is yours.

verse.meaning: Arjuna asks why he must act at all if understanding is higher. Krishna says no one can stop acting, that repressing the body while the mind indulges is self-deception, and that action beats inaction. Doing your allotted work is better than doing nothing, because even the maintenance of your body would not be possible without action.
verse.for_you: You are looking for a calm start, but the mind that won't settle is still a mind that is moving. The work you do each day is already keeping the body alive, and it is also the ground where a clear mind can begin.
verse.try_today: Before you begin your work, take one minute to feel the weight of what you are about to do.
verse.scene_line: You are standing at the edge of your work, and the question is how to step in.
asks: How can my work be the place where I rest?
What does it mean to do my work without running from it?
How do I tell the difference between action and escape?

story.title: Arjuna asks to see the cosmic form
story.story_hook: His confusion gone, Arjuna made a bold request of his friend: show me who you really are.
story.summary: Thanking Krishna for dispelling his confusion, Arjuna asks to see his imperishable form if he is able.
story.lesson: Ask humbly for what you long to see.

story.hook_title: Arjuna asked his best friend Krishna to show who he really was
story.teaser: Arjuna asked his best friend Krishna to show who he really was
story.for_you: The mind that would not settle asked for a vision of everything. Now you are left with the ordinary morning, the inbox, the quiet before the day. That is where your part is. You do not need to see the whole picture to begin.
asks: How do I let go of the whole picture?
How do I hold only my small part today?
